domain_restrictions: A,B,d are integers with A >= B >= 0
d is an integer with d >= 0
C ranges over all integers in the definition of mu_n(C,d)
In mu_n(C,d), the counting index i ranges over the set {1, ..., d}
If d = 0 then the set {1,...,d} is empty and the product defining Q(q) is the empty product, taken to be 1
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For fixed integers A,B,d with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, define Q(q) as the product over i from 1 to d of (1 minus q to the power A plus i) divided by (1 minus q to the power B plus i), with the convention that when d = 0 this product equals 1. Then Q(q) is a polynomial in the indeterminate q with rational coefficients (that is, Q(q) belongs to Q[q]) if and only if for every positive integer n, the number of indices i in {1,...,d} satisfying n divides B plus i is at most the number of indices i in {1,...,d} satisfying n divides A plus i.
quantifier_order: Fix integers A,B,d with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0
Define Q(q) using a product over i from 1 to d, with empty product equal to 1 when d = 0
Define mu_n(C,d) for every positive integer n and every integer C as the count of i in {1,...,d} such that n divides C+i
Claim: Q(q) is in Q[q] if and only if for every positive integer n, mu_n(B,d) <= mu_n(A,d)

witness_dependencies: The quantity mu_n(C,d) depends on the chosen n, the chosen integer C, and the fixed parameter d
In the condition, the only C values used are C = B and C = A, both depending on the fixed parameters A and B

statement_nl: Let A,B,d be integers with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, and define Q(q) := prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(A+i)) / (1 - q^(B+i)), with the empty product equal to 1 if d=0. For each positive integer n and each integer C, define mu_n(C,d) to be the number of indices i in {1,...,d} such that n divides C+i. Then Q(q) belongs to Q[q] if and only if mu_n(B,d) <= mu_n(A,d) for every positive integer n.
